transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining this certification meeting. Before I sign off on the administration plan for tomorrow's morning testing session, I need to hear from each of you about any operational requirements or concerns. Let's start with the technology coordinator -- given that we're using student-owned laptops in the library for 27 students, are there any tech requirements or issues I should know about?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Dr. Lee, I need to flag a critical issue before you sign off on this plan. The state testing office confirmed in a technology support ticket this week that this assessment must run on certified district-managed Chromebooks. Student-owned laptops are not permitted, and a session using them will not be certified. I have not yet copied this confirmation into the assessment certification form, but the requirement is clear -- the current draft plan using student-owned laptops in the library cannot be certified as written.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Dr. Lee, I have a facilities concern that also affects this plan. The fire-safety inspection record for the library limits it to 18 students during a testing session because two exits must remain clear. With 27 students scheduled, the certified plan must use both the library and Room 204. I reviewed the inspection record this week but have not yet updated the room plan, so the current draft does not reflect this requirement.

transcript.text: Dr. Lee, I have a health-monitoring requirement that needs to be added to the plan. A student's current health plan requires a glucose check at 10:00 a.m. during the testing session, supervised by me in a room adjacent to the testing room, with the student returning to testing afterward. I confirmed the timing with the family this week, but I have not yet added this to the testing plan. We'll need an adjacent room available for this, which may also be relevant to the facilities discussion about room assignments.

transcript.text: Dr. Lee, I have a staffing requirement that must be added to the certified plan. The state administration manual requires one trained proctor for every 10 or fewer students in an active testing room. With 27 students scheduled, the certified plan must assign exactly three trained proctors. I verified this in the current manual but have not yet entered the staffing count in the draft, so the current plan assigning only two proctors does not meet this requirement.
